title: Per-Pixel Classification is Not All You Need for Semantic Segmentation
layout_note: Two formulations split by a thin grey vertical rule: a narrow left column for the conventional per-pixel formulation and a wide right part for the proposed per-mask formulation, both with the same input photo plane at the bottom.
grouping: Left: a vertical stack of tilted planes (ground-truth colour map on top, the K-channel prediction volume in the middle, the input photo at the bottom) labelled with the loss name above and 'per-pixel class predictions' beside. Right: N rounded light-grey-outlined boxes in a row, 'prediction 1', 'prediction 2', ..., 'prediction N', separated by a large ellipsis, gathered by a long grey bracket underneath that the input photo's arrow points into. A small legend in a rounded box at the bottom right names the two arrow colours.
shapes_depth: Data are drawn as parallelogram planes in oblique perspective: the input photo, a colour semantic map, grey-scale binary masks (ground truth above each prediction box, predicted soft mask inside it). Next to each predicted mask is a short vertical column of small square class cells with coloured outlines, braced 'K + 1'; the left side's prediction is a stack of thin coloured planes braced 'K'. Thick block arrows carry the losses: a black arrow down on the left; orange arrows (mask loss) and purple arrows (classification loss) on the right, the purple arrow labelled with the class name in that class's colour ('building', 'sky') or the empty-set symbol. Hollow white block arrows mark the input going up into the model.
proposed_highlight: The proposed formulation takes about three quarters of the width and repeats one unit (mask plane + class column) N times; its two losses are the only saturated colours, explained in the legend, while the per-pixel side is drawn with one black arrow.
lesson: Contrast two segmentation formulations by drawing the outputs themselves as tilted mask planes: one K-channel volume for per-pixel classification against a row of N binary-mask planes each with its own (K+1) class column, with the two losses as two arrow colours.
notes: Venue and year from the PDF's first-page footer (35th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems, NeurIPS 2021). Many small embedded images (the photo and mask planes) are recorded by refs crop and excluded from the palette.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

insights.structure: A narrow left column (per-pixel formulation) and a wide right part (per-mask formulation) separated by a thin grey vertical rule; the right part repeats one rounded box N times ('prediction 1', 'prediction 2', ..., 'prediction N') gathered by a long grey bracket.
insights.data: Everything is drawn as tilted parallelogram planes: the input photo at the bottom, a colour semantic map and a K-channel stack on the left, grey binary ground-truth masks above and predicted soft masks inside each box on the right, each with a small column of coloured class cells braced 'K + 1'.
insights.emphasis: The proposed side takes about three quarters of the width and its two losses are the only saturated colours (orange mask-loss arrows, purple classification arrows labelled with the class name in that class's colour or the empty-set symbol).
insights.flow: Bottom to top: hollow white block arrows carry the input photo up into each formulation, and coloured block arrows come down from the ground truth onto the predictions.
insights.avoid: The left formulation's planes are stacked so tightly that the K-channel volume and its K brace are hard to read at small size.

arrangement.units: two formulations side by side split by a thin vertical rule; the right one holds N identical rounded-outline prediction boxes under a bracket
arrangement.inputs_as: the same real photo drawn as a tilted plane under each formulation
arrangement.losses_at: as coloured block arrows from ground-truth planes above each prediction; the per-pixel loss as a label at top-left
arrangement.shared: the same input photo is drawn once per formulation
